summary: Quorum's admin Design Lab (site/src/components/admin/design-lab-*, about 1,000 lines of components plus 1,000 of lib) lets the owner pick an article, see one slide on a stage at most 480 px wide for 4:5 (72 px thumbnails underneath), switch among five canvases, pick one of five launch looks from a strip of real cover renders, fine-tune a recipe (A/B colour variant, photo treatment none/mono/duotone, type scale 90/100/110 %), edit one free-text field per slide (30-word cap) and export PNGs or a Canva brief. Every slide image is a server render of the article deck (renderCarouselSlidePng, cached privately for 300 s). Every chip click and text save writes a JSON file to Quorum's main branch through the GitHub Contents API: 79 'set the deck design' commits exist, 45 of them for one article. It works on article summary decks only; the DNESKAi photo kit (renderDneskaiSlide) is never called from site/, and nothing binds a choice to an exact-bytes approval. There is no keyboard handling. Reusable for an OwnDashboard Design Lab: the look-strip pattern (all looks rendered side by side as real covers), the stage-plus-strip layout, the canvas chips idea, per-field problem display from the package workspace, and its e2e/axe checks. Not reusable: GitHub persistence, the article/recipe model, free-text-per-slide editing, mono/duotone treatments, and the Canva hand-off.

files.role: Client constants: 5 canvases, launch/legacy families, look labels, treatments, scales, 30-word cap, slide URL and Canva brief builders.
Article rail, stage, slide strip, look strip, export footer; auto-saves recipe on every chip click.
Text / Vzhled / Canva tabs: one textarea per slide, recipe chips, presets, Canva brief.
Package decks: per-slide headline/body/alt/code fields with per-field problems, Send to Queue.
Brand tab: kit logos on grounds, rules, doNots, socialRules list.
POST: save recipe, slide text or preset through the admin store.
Persistence: GitHub Contents API PUT to lukaskourilcz/quorum main (or local file without a token).
Server read model: LabArticle from stored article summaries, recipes, presets and text overrides.
Renders one slide PNG of an article deck per request; private, max-age=300.
E2E: Design Lab workspace and Brand tab, axe checks across themes and widths.

facts.fact: Five canvases are offered: Instagram 4:5 (master), square, story 9:16, Threads and LinkedIn square; a canvas a template does not declare is refused by the render route with 422.
Five launch looks folio, press, rail, fault, halo with Czech one-line descriptions; 25 legacy families behind a disclosure.
Recipe chips: colour variant A/B (B sets accentSwap), photo treatment none/mono/duotone, type scale 0.9/1/1.1; presets can be saved.
Stage: one slide image, max width min(520, 600 x ratio) px, i.e. 480 px for 4:5; slide strip thumbnails 72 px wide; look strip cards 144-160 px wide, each a real render of slide 1 in that look.
Navigation is by buttons only (previous/next slide, slide strip, article rail); no component in design-lab-* registers a keyboard handler.

A chip click updates the recipe and, when writes are enabled, immediately POSTs it; the store PUTs the JSON file to GitHub (repository default lukaskourilcz/quorum, branch default main) and returns the commit. Without a token on Vercel it refuses with UNCONFIGURED.
Text editing is one free textarea per slide with a 30-word cap; the preview updates only after 'Uložit slide'.

The Lab works on article summary decks (LabArticle built from stored article packages, buildArticleDeck/derivedCopyPack); no file under site/ calls renderDneskaiSlide, validateDneskaiSlide or DNESKAI_PHOTO_TEMPLATES.
Approval is outside the Lab: edits create a draft in Quorum's Queue and 'every publication needs its own approval and a connected social profile'; nothing hashes the rendered bytes.
The Canva tab builds a brief with every slide's text, canvas size, palette, fonts and photo credit and names instagram.com/technology as the visual reference.

Tests: 6 workspace component tests, 2 bilingual, 2 WebDev Signal, 27 lib tests (brand 5, families 2, package 9, tehdejsi 1, ventures 10) plus e2e for the workspace and Brand tab with axe across themes and widths.

findings.recommendation: Do not port the store. In OwnDashboard keep the chosen kit as a row (or a deck field per approval-06) and only persist on an explicit choice; previews are ephemeral.
findings.impactStatement: Trying looks pollutes git history, needs a GitHub token on the deployment and a network round trip per click; in OwnDashboard a merge to main deploys production, so this persistence model must not be ported.

findings.title: No keyboard flow
findings.claim: Slides, looks and articles are changed only by clicking buttons; no design-lab component handles key events.

findings.recommendation: Design the OwnDashboard Lab keyboard-first: ←/→ slides, ↑/↓ posts, 1-5 kits, E edit, A approve (with the exact-bytes confirmation), all announced and documented, respecting WCAG 2.2 (no single-key shortcuts without a way to turn them off or remap).
findings.impactStatement: For 4 posts x 7 slides x 5 kits a day, arrow keys, 1-5 for kits and one approve key would save the owner a few minutes daily and fit the under-10-minutes goal.

truth.evidence: grep onKeyDown|keydown in design-lab-* is empty; navigation via buttons at :110-112.

impact.reason: Keyboard flow is a direct owner-minute saving at 4 posts a day.

findings.recommendation: In OwnDashboard, any kit or text change produces a new revision whose rendered bytes the owner approves; the Lab shows the hash state ('changed since approval') next to the approve button.
findings.impactStatement: A port that kept 'save look = done' would let a kit switch slip past the hard rule that approval binds exact bytes.
